newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty straddles resistance, eyes upside.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty straddles resistance, eyes upside.

text.p: The Polish zloty straddled resistance without much impetus to edge higher in early Wednesday trade but dealers said the zloty may later in the day build up enough steam to test central bank intervention levels.
Dealers said that some foreign entry into Polish paper as well as other capital inflows were likely to keep the zloty pressing against strong resistance at 1.5 percent from parity.
"The zloty could drift (sideways today), but it may edge higher as there seem to be more (currency sell) offers on the market," said Leszek Szafranek, dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
At 0835 GMT the zloty was at 1.53/1.49 percent from the parity rate, against 1.56/1.50 percent at 0700 GMT.
It was at 3.2175/85 to the dollar against opening's 3.2195/15 and at 1.8812/22 to the mark against 1.8785/95.
On the money market one-day rates eased slightly under weight of Wedneday's 578 million zloty net inflow as banks already secured cash for T-bills bought on Monday.
Overnight rates slipped to 22.20/22.40 percent from opening's 22.30/22.60 percent while tomorrow/next eased to 22.22/50 from 22.35/22.55.
